title: It’s Not Easy Being a Tang Dynasty Dog!
synopsis: Learn about the incredibly detailed Tang Dynasty laws regarding dogs.

fullText.simplified:
唐朝的狗，不好当啊！

    中国有这样一种说法：“宁为太平犬，不为乱世人”，用来告诫人们珍惜和平。那么，在和平了几百年的唐朝做条狗，应该是很容易的吧？那你就大错特错了！
    在唐朝，想当一条好狗，必须得遵纪守法，首要任务就是管住嘴。如果不小心咬伤了人，就只能接受法律的制裁了。重视法律的唐朝人，在编撰法典《唐律》时，不仅对人与人之间的违法行为进行了详细的规定，对极其容易引发邻里纠纷的狗咬人案件也进行了详细的处理规定。
    那么，唐朝的狗需要遵守什么样的法律呢？
    在唐代，如果出现狗咬人的事件，判案之前首先需要确认属于哪种情况：是狗主动攻击人、人明知狗咬人而管不好、人故意放狗咬还是被咬的人故意逗狗而被咬。确定属于哪种情况以后，对人和狗的处理就好办了，只要翻开《唐律》就能找到合适的处理办法。
    对于经常惹是生非的狗，它们往往属于主动攻击人的类型。对于这样的狗，唐朝律令处理态度之坚决，手段之严厉，让现在的动物保护者绝对无法理解。在这种情况下，行人是没有责任的，狗要承担全部的法律责任。《唐律》规定，对于这样的狗，人们要用剪刀把它的两只耳朵剪掉，以此进行惩罚。
    当然，更多的狗咬人事件责任并不完全都在狗，而是狗的主人没有管理好自己的狗。凡是这种情况，狗和狗的主人都要承担相应的法律责任。《唐律》规定：由于养狗者的过失而导致狗咬人的，则各自根据其罪责予以赔偿。所以养狗要拴好，否则，如果出现狗伤人事件，人和狗都不能逃脱罪责。狗和主人会各被打四十棍子，主人还可能需要进行额外的财产赔偿。
    还有一种极端恶劣的情况，就是养狗的人故意放狗咬死咬伤人。《唐律》为此专门设置了一条惩处的条款叫“故放令杀伤人”。故意放狗者，会被判处类似于现代的伤害致死罪的罪责。而这种情形中有一个比较有意思的规定细则：故意放狗的人，有二十天的保辜期。如果被咬的人在这一期限内死亡，放狗的人要承担杀人的刑事责任；而被咬的人如果在这一期限内没有死亡，或者因为其他原因死亡的，伤人者只要承担伤人的刑事责任。有些类似我们当代的取保候审制度，不禁让人感叹唐代法律的严谨程度之高。
    当然，制定《唐律》的人考虑得非常细致。如果狗因为生病，在看病过程中失控咬人，是不需要接受惩罚的。但这也分情况：如果是主人花钱雇人给狗看病，兽医不小心被咬伤，养狗的人则不需要承担责任；而如果是不花钱请人为狗看病而被咬伤的，狗的主人则要依法予以赔偿。当然，一些无聊的人逗狗玩儿时而被咬伤的，狗和狗的主人也不需要承担任何法律责任。　　
    狗咬人本是生活中一件再平常不过的事情，而唐朝法律对处理此类案件却规定得如此详细，并照顾到了人与人、人与狗之间的各种权利，也明确了各方该承担的责任。这样说来，在唐朝做条狗也不容易啊！
fullText.traditional:
唐朝的狗，不好當啊！

    中國有這樣一種說法：“寧為太平犬，不為亂世人”，用來告誡人們珍惜和平。那麼，在和平了幾百年的唐朝做條狗，應該是很容易的吧？那你就大錯特錯了！
    在唐朝，想當一條好狗，必須得遵紀守法，首要任務就是管住嘴。如果不小心咬傷了人，就只能接受法律的制裁了。重視法律的唐朝人，在編撰法典《唐律》時，不僅對人與人之間的違法行為進行了詳細的規定，對極其容易引發鄰里糾紛的狗咬人案件也進行了詳細的處理規定。
    那麼，唐朝的狗需要遵守什麼樣的法律呢？
    在唐代，如果出現狗咬人的事件，判案之前首先需要確認屬於哪種情況：是狗主動攻擊人、人明知狗咬人而管不好、人故意放狗咬還是被咬的人故意逗狗而被咬。確定屬於哪種情況以後，對人和狗的處理就好辦了，只要翻開《唐律》就能找到合適的處理辦法。
    對於經常惹是生非的狗，它們往往屬於主動攻擊人的類型。對於這樣的狗，唐朝律令處理態度之堅決，手段之嚴厲，讓現在的動物保護者絕對無法理解。在這種情況下，行人是沒有責任的，狗要承擔全部的法律責任。《唐律》規定，對於這樣的狗，人們要用剪刀把它的兩隻耳朵剪掉，以此進行懲罰。
    當然，更多的狗咬人事件責任並不完全都在狗，而是狗的主人沒有管理好自己的狗。凡是這種情況，狗和狗的主人都要承擔相應的法律責任。《唐律》規定：由於養狗者的過失而導致狗咬人的，則各自根據其罪責予以賠償。所以養狗要拴好，否則，如果出現狗傷人事件，人和狗都不能逃脫罪責。狗和主人會各被打四十棍子，主人還可能需要進行額外的財產賠償。
    還有一種極端惡劣的情況，就是養狗的人故意放狗咬死咬傷人。《唐律》為此專門設置了一條懲處的條款叫“故放令殺傷人”。故意放狗者，會被判處類似於現代的傷害致死罪的罪責。而這種情形中有一個比較有意思的規定細則：故意放狗的人，有二十天的保辜期。如果被咬的人在這一期限內死亡，放狗的人要承擔殺人的刑事責任；而被咬的人如果在這一期限內沒有死亡，或者因為其他原因死亡的，傷人者只要承擔傷人的刑事責任。有些類似我們當代的取保候審制度，不禁讓人感嘆唐代法律的嚴謹程度之高。
    當然，制定《唐律》的人考慮得非常細緻。如果狗因為生病，在看病過程中失控咬人，是不需要接受懲罰的。但這也分情況：如果是主人花錢雇人給狗看病，獸醫不小心被咬傷，養狗的人則不需要承擔責任；而如果是不花錢請人為狗看病而被咬傷的，狗的主人則要依法予以賠償。當然，一些無聊的人逗狗玩兒時而被咬傷的，狗和狗的主人也不需要承擔任何法律責任。　　
    狗咬人本是生活中一件再平常不過的事情，而唐朝法律對處理此類案件卻規定得如此詳細，並照顧到了人與人、人與狗之間的各種權利，也明確了各方該承擔的責任。這樣說來，在唐朝做條狗也不容易啊！

sentences.traditional: 主人還可能需要進行額外的財產賠償。
sentences.pinyin: zhǔ rén hái kě néng xū yào jìn xíng é wài de cái chǎn péi cháng
sentences.english: Both the dog and the owner will be hit forty times with a stick.
The owner may also need to provide additional monetary compensation.

sentences.simplified: 还有一种极端恶劣的情况，就是养狗的人故意放狗咬死咬伤人。
sentences.traditional: 還有一種極端惡劣的情況，就是養狗的人故意放狗咬死咬傷人。
sentences.pinyin: hái yǒu yì zhǒng jí duān è liè de qíng kuàng jiù shì yǎng gǒu de rén gù yì fàng gǒu yǎo sǐ yǎo shāng rén

sentences.simplified: 《唐律》为此专门设置了一条惩处的条款叫“故放令杀伤人”。
sentences.traditional: 《唐律》為此專門設置了一條懲處的條款叫“故放令殺傷人”。
sentences.pinyin: táng lǜ wèi cǐ zhuān mén shè zhì le yì tiáo chéng chǔ de tiáo kuǎn jiào gù fàng lìng shā shāng rén
sentences.english: There is also an extreme situation when the owner intentionally releases a dog to bite and kill or wound others.

sentences.simplified: 故意放狗者，会被判处类似于现代的伤害致死罪的罪责。
sentences.traditional: 故意放狗者，會被判處類似於現代的傷害致死罪的罪責。
sentences.pinyin: gù yì fàng gǒu zhě huì bèi pàn chǔ lèi sì yú xiàn dài de shāng hài zhì sǐ zuì de zuì zé
sentences.english: The Tang Code set up a punishment clause called “intentionally releasing to kill or wound a person” especially for this.

sentences.simplified: 而这种情形中有一个比较有意思的规定细则：
sentences.traditional: 而這種情形中有一個比較有意思的規定細則：
sentences.pinyin: ér zhè zhǒng qíng xing zhōng yǒu yí ge bǐ jiào yǒu yì si de guī dìng xì zé
sentences.english: The person who intentionally releases the dog would be convicted of a crime similar to the current “intentional injury resulting in death”.

sentences.simplified: 故意放狗的人，有二十天的保辜期。
sentences.traditional: 故意放狗的人，有二十天的保辜期。
sentences.pinyin: gù yì fàng gǒu de rén yǒu èr shí tiān de bǎo gū qī
sentences.english: Yet there was an interesting rule in such cases.

sentences.simplified: 如果被咬的人在这一期限内死亡，放狗的人要承担杀人的刑事责任；
sentences.traditional: 如果被咬的人在這一期限內死亡，放狗的人要承擔殺人的刑事責任；
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ bèi yǎo de rén zài zhè yì qī xiàn nèi sǐ wáng fàng gǒu de rén yào chéng dān shā rén de xíng shì zé rèn
sentences.english: A person who intentionally released a dog had a 20-day time limit of culpability

sentences.simplified: 而被咬的人如果在这一期限内没有死亡，或者因为其他原因死亡的，
sentences.traditional: 而被咬的人如果在這一期限內沒有死亡，或者因為其他原因死亡的，
sentences.pinyin: ér bèi yǎo de rén rú guǒ zài zhè yì qī xiàn nèi méi yǒu sǐ wáng huò zhě yīn wèi qí tā yuán yīn sǐ wáng de
sentences.english: If the victim died within this period, the person who released the dog needed to bear criminal liability for murder.

sentences.simplified: 伤人者只要承担伤人的刑事责任。
sentences.traditional: 傷人者只要承擔傷人的刑事責任。
sentences.pinyin: shāng rén zhě zhǐ yào chéng dān shāng rén de xíng shì zé rèn
sentences.english: If the victim did not die within this period or died from another cause, ..

sentences.simplified: 有些类似我们当代的取保候审制度，
sentences.traditional: 有些類似我們當代的取保候審制度，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu xiē lèi sì wǒ men dāng dài de qǔ bǎo hòu shěn zhì dù
sentences.english: .. the accused only need to bear criminal liability for causing injury.

sentences.simplified: 不禁让人感叹唐代法律的严谨程度之高。
sentences.traditional: 不禁讓人感嘆唐代法律的嚴謹程度之高。
sentences.pinyin: bù jīn ràng rén gǎn tàn táng dài fǎ lǜ de yán jǐn chéng dù zhī gāo
sentences.english: There are some similarities to our present day system of bail pending trial.
One can’t help but marvel at the level of legal rigor during the Tang Dynasty.

sentences.simplified: 当然，制定《唐律》的人考虑得非常细致。
sentences.traditional: 當然，制定《唐律》的人考慮得非常細緻。
sentences.pinyin: dāng rán zhì dìng táng lǜ de rén kǎo lǜ de fēi cháng xì zhì

sentences.simplified: 如果狗因为生病，在看病过程中失控咬人，
sentences.traditional: 如果狗因為生病，在看病過程中失控咬人，
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ gǒu yīn wèi shēng bìng zài kàn bìng guò chéng zhōng shī kòng yǎo rén
sentences.english: Of course, the people who formulated the Tang Code were extremely meticulous.

sentences.simplified: 是不需要接受惩罚的。
sentences.traditional: 是不需要接受懲罰的。
sentences.pinyin: shì bù xū yào jiē shòu chéng fá de
sentences.english: If a dog was sick and bit someone after losing control while receiving treatment, ..

sentences.simplified: 但这也分情况：
sentences.traditional: 但這也分情況：
sentences.pinyin: dàn zhè yě fēn qíng kuàng
sentences.english: .. there was no need for the dog to be punished.

sentences.simplified: 如果是主人花钱雇人给狗看病，兽医不小心被咬伤，
sentences.traditional: 如果是主人花錢雇人給狗看病，獸醫不小心被咬傷，
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ shì zhǔ rén huā qián gù rén gěi gǒu kàn bìng shòu yī bù xiǎo xīn bèi yǎo shāng
sentences.english: But this also depended on the situation.

sentences.simplified: 养狗的人则不需要承担责任；
sentences.traditional: 養狗的人則不需要承擔責任；
sentences.pinyin: yǎng gǒu de rén zé bù xū yào chéng dān zé rèn
sentences.english: If the owner paid for someone to give the dog a check up and the vet was accidentally bitten, ..

sentences.simplified: 而如果是不花钱请人为狗看病而被咬伤的，
sentences.traditional: 而如果是不花錢請人為狗看病而被咬傷的，
sentences.pinyin: ér rú guǒ shì bù huā qián qǐng rén wèi gǒu kàn bìng ér bèi yǎo shāng de
sentences.english: .. the dog owner did not need to bear liability.

sentences.simplified: 狗的主人则要依法予以赔偿。
sentences.traditional: 狗的主人則要依法予以賠償。
sentences.pinyin: gǒu de zhǔ rén zé yào yī fǎ yǔ yǐ péi cháng
sentences.english: But, if the person giving the dog a check up wasn’t paid and got bitten, ..

sentences.simplified: 当然，一些无聊的人逗狗玩儿时而被咬伤的，
sentences.traditional: 當然，一些無聊的人逗狗玩兒時而被咬傷的，
sentences.pinyin: dāng rán yì xiē wú liáo de rén dòu gǒu wán'r shí ér bèi yǎo shāng de
sentences.english: .. then the dog owner needed to pay compensation according to the law.

sentences.simplified: 狗和狗的主人也不需要承担任何法律责任。
sentences.traditional: 狗和狗的主人也不需要承擔任何法律責任。
sentences.pinyin: gǒu hé gǒu de zhǔ rén yě bù xū yào chéng dān rèn hé fǎ lǜ zé rèn
sentences.english: Of course, some senseless people got bitten after provoking dogs for fun.
In these cases, neither the dog nor the owner needed to bear legal liability.

sentences.simplified: 狗咬人本是生活中一件再平常不过的事情，
sentences.traditional: 狗咬人本是生活中一件再平常不過的事情，
sentences.pinyin: gǒu yǎo rén běn shì shēng huó zhōng yí jiàn zài píng cháng bú guò de shì qing

sentences.simplified: 而唐朝法律对处理此类案件却规定得如此详细，
sentences.traditional: 而唐朝法律對處理此類案件卻規定得如此詳細，
sentences.pinyin: ér táng cháo fǎ lǜ duì chǔ lǐ cǐ lèi àn jiàn què guī dìng de rú cǐ xiáng xì
sentences.english: Cases of dogs biting are extremely common.

sentences.simplified: 并照顾到了人与人、人与狗之间的各种权利，
sentences.traditional: 並照顧到了人與人、人與狗之間的各種權利，
sentences.pinyin: bìng zhào gù dào le rén yǔ rén rén yǔ gǒu zhī jiān de gè zhǒng quán lì
sentences.english: Yet, the detailed regulations of Tang dynasty law for dealing with such cases ..

sentences.simplified: 也明确了各方该承担的责任。
sentences.traditional: 也明確了各方該承擔的責任。
sentences.pinyin: yě míng què le gè fāng gāi chéng dān de zé rèn
sentences.english: .. took into consideration the various rights between people, and also between people and dogs.

sentences.simplified: 这样说来，在唐朝做条狗也不容易啊！
sentences.traditional: 這樣說來，在唐朝做條狗也不容易啊！
sentences.pinyin: zhè yàng shuō lái zài táng cháo zuò tiáo gǒu yě bù róng yì a
sentences.english: They also clearly specified the legal responsibilities of each party.
We can conclude that being a dog during the Tang dynasty wasn’t easy!

raw.synopsis: Learn about the incredibly detailed Tang Dynasty laws regarding dogs.
sentence_translations: It’s Not Easy Being a Tang Dynasty Dog!
In China there is a saying that goes, “Better a dog in peaceful times than a human in troubled times,” ..
.. which is used to admonish people to treasure peace.
Then, it must have been very easy to be a dog in the Tang dynasty which was peaceful for several hundred years, right?
Oh, you‘d be so wrong!
During the Tang Dynasty, to be a good dog, you had to obey the law. The most important task was controlling your mouth.
If a dog accidentally bit and injured someone, the only option was to accept the punishment as set by the law.
People of the Tang dynasty placed great value on the law.
When compiling the Tang Code, ..
.. not only did they set out detailed regulations regarding illegal activity between humans, ..
.. they also detailed provisions for dealing with cases of dogs biting people, which were especially common causes of neighborhood disputes.
Then, what kind of laws did the dogs of the Tang dynasty need to follow?
In the Tang dynasty, if there was a case of a dog biting someone, ..
.. the type of situation needed to be confirmed before a verdict was reached.
Whether it was the dog that initiated and attacked someone, ..
someone knew a dog would bite but didn’t control the dog properly, ..
.. someone intentionally released the dog to bite, or that someone got bitten because he intentionally provoked the dog.
After confirming the type of situation, dealing with the person and the dog was easy.
One only needed to open up the Tang Code to find the appropriate processes.
Dogs that were constantly making trouble often fell into the category of dogs that initiated attacks on people.
The resolute attitude and harsh means for dealing with this type of dog in Tang laws and statues, ..
.. definitely would not be understood by today’s animal rights supporters.
In these circumstances, the person had no fault; the dog had to accept all legal liability.
The Tang Code says that this type of dog must be punished by cutting both of its ears off.
Of course, most cases of dogs biting people weren’t completely the dog’s fault.
Rather, the owner didn’t properly control the dog.
In these cases, both the dog and the owner needed to bear the corresponding legal liability.
The Tang Code states: because the owner’s mistakes caused the dog to bite someone, ..
..  both have to give compensation according to their guilt.
So, dogs must be tied up ..
.. otherwise, if a dog injures someone, neither the owner nor the dog can escape liability of the offense.
Both the dog and the owner will be hit forty times with a stick.
The owner may also need to provide additional monetary compensation.
There is also an extreme situation when the owner intentionally releases a dog to bite and kill or wound others.
The Tang Code set up a punishment clause called “intentionally releasing to kill or wound a person” especially for this.
The person who intentionally releases the dog would be convicted of a crime similar to the current “intentional injury resulting in death”.
Yet there was an interesting rule in such cases.
A person who intentionally released a dog had a 20-day time limit of culpability
If the victim died within this period, the person who released the dog needed to bear criminal liability for murder.
If the victim did not die within this period or died from another cause, ..
.. the accused only need to bear criminal liability for causing injury.
There are some similarities to our present day system of bail pending trial.
One can’t help but marvel at the level of legal rigor during the Tang Dynasty.
Of course, the people who formulated the Tang Code were extremely meticulous.
If a dog was sick and bit someone after losing control while receiving treatment, ..
.. there was no need for the dog to be punished.
But this also depended on the situation.
If the owner paid for someone to give the dog a check up and the vet was accidentally bitten, ..
.. the dog owner did not need to bear liability.
But, if the person giving the dog a check up wasn’t paid and got bitten, ..
.. then the dog owner needed to pay compensation according to the law.
Of course, some senseless people got bitten after provoking dogs for fun.
In these cases, neither the dog nor the owner needed to bear legal liability.
Cases of dogs biting are extremely common.
Yet, the detailed regulations of Tang dynasty law for dealing with such cases ..
.. took into consideration the various rights between people, and also between people and dogs.
They also clearly specified the legal responsibilities of each party.
We can conclude that being a dog during the Tang dynasty wasn’t easy!
